title: The Job Nobody Wants in Japan
text: It's impossible to get fired in Japan, but companies found something way worse. Imagine your boss walks you past your desk to a tiny room with no computer and no work. Just a ticking clock and a guy [music] with his feet up scrolling on his phone like he's on vacation. "Your new job," your boss says, "is nothing. Just sit here until 6:00." And you're thinking, "Wait, I'm getting paid for this?" At first, it's paradise. Then, your coworker starts staring when you walk past. The emails stop, and your old desk already has someone else's family photos on it. Every Friday, your boss pops his head in with a big smile to ask how you're enjoying your new role. Still, the guy in the corner has been doing [music] this for 3 years and looks happier than anyone in the building. So, if they want to pay you to do nothing, fine. You kick your feet up right next to him. Then, one Monday, you walk in and he's gone. His chair is pushed in, his desk is cleared, [music] and nobody will tell you where he went. You see, Japanese law makes it almost impossible to fire someone, but there's no law against making them miserable. So, they take away your work and your friends and just wait, because nobody can do nothing forever.

title: How a Mirror Rigged a Horse Race
text: He bet his life savings on the slowest horse in the race. The whole betting room is laughing at him because all day long he hasn't bet a single dollar. He just sits by the window smiling because he has a mirror. Wait, what's a mirror going to do? Well, the racetrack is right over the hill from town and his buddy is up on that hill with the biggest mirror he could find. Race after race the favorite wins and the hill stays dark. And by the fifth the regulars are betting on whether he'll ever bet. Hey mirror man, maybe try wiping it. In the last race the favorite's so far ahead it's jockey is waving [music] to his mom and horse nine is so far behind it's practically in the parking lot. Then the hill flashes and he puts every dollar he has on horse nine. The guy behind the counter almost feels bad taking it. Pal, that horse lost a race to the milk cart and it [music] was pulling the milk cart. You see, back then betting rooms didn't find out who won until the winner came clicking in over a wire and until it did bets stayed open. Up on that hill his buddy just watched horse nine come out of nowhere and steal it by a nose. So, while the room is still laughing the wire starts clicking and by the time it spells out nine nobody's laughing anymore.

title: Why Perfect Railroads Don't Work
text: He saw gaps into a railroad every 39 feet. You see, two companies are racing to build a railroad along a canyon so deep you can't see the bottom. And whoever finishes first gets the whole country's business. He's the youngest engineer on the job. And when his boss sees a finger-wide gap between every single rail, his face goes purple. You're wrecking my railroad. But he won't close a single one. The other company lays their rails end-to-end, perfectly smooth and finishes first. Their trains glide across the canyon without a sound, while his go clickety-clack over every gap. [music] The newspapers start calling it the clickety-clack line, and everyone switches to the quiet trains. Then summer comes, and something weird happens. His gaps start shrinking. In May, you can fit a coin in them. By July, barely a sheet of paper. And his boss is thrilled. See? Even your gaps know you were wrong. Meanwhile, on the perfect [music] railroad, the rails have started groaning in the afternoon sun, pushing against each other like they want to get out. On the hottest day anyone can remember, his gaps finally close, rail touching rail. [music] And halfway across the canyon, the perfect railroad kicks sideways like a snake right as a train rolls onto it.

title: The Science Behind Slot Machines
text: You just watched two jackpot [music] symbols land and the third one stopped one click short. So, you moved to the machine next door and the exact same thing happens. Your buddy leans over and says, "Bro, it's just warming [music] up." So, you put in another hundred, but it's starting to feel like the machine is teasing you on purpose. So, let's crack it open. Inside is a list of every place that last reel can stop. The jackpot is on that list once. One click short is on there over and over. So, every time you spin, the machine is way more likely to stop one click short than on the jackpot.

title: He Could Spot Winning Tickets Just by Looking
text: Look at these two scratch cards. One's a winner, and one's garbage. Yet, there's a way to tell without scratching either of them. It all started when a guy got fired and spent five bucks on two scratch cards on the way home. He scratches one and wins his five bucks back, but instead of celebrating like a normal person, he gets suspicious. If the lottery decides exactly how many winners get printed, how does the machine know which ones they are? So, he does what any sane person would do. He blows his entire severance check on a huge stack, spreads them across his apartment floor, and stares until something jumps out. Every card has little grids of numbers printed right on the front, and most of the numbers show up two or three times, but a few only show up once. And whenever [music] three of those loners line up in a row, it's a winner, which means this guy just cracked the lottery. He could walk into every gas station in the state and clean them out. So, what does he do? He calls the lottery. "Sir, that's impossible." Okay, so he walks into their office with a box full of cards he's never scratched, [music] sorted into winners and losers, and gets 90%of them right. By the end of the week, the game is gone from every store.

title: What the Grave Bell Really Meant
text: They buried a man alive with a bell tied to his finger. You see, people were so scared of waking up in a coffin that graves came with a little bell on top, tied by a string to the body's finger. Except when his bell starts ringing at 2:00 in the morning, the guy next door decides it's probably the wind. Then it rings faster, and now the whole street is out on their porches going, "You go check. No, you go check." Somebody drags the doctor out of bed, and he goes, "Bodies twitch. He's dead. I signed the paper myself." But his wife isn't on her porch. She's sitting in the dark with the shovel by the door because she knows that ring. Three short, one long, the exact signal they practiced. Wait, practiced? Well, he was never dead. He owed money to half the town, so he faked his death, and the second that bell rang, she was supposed to grab the shovel, [music] dig him up, and skip town with him. Instead, she just sits there all night listening to it ring fast, then slow, then once every few minutes until sunrise, when it finally stops. You see, with him in the ground, every debt got buried right along with him, and the house was all hers.

title: The Pink Prison Cell Experiment
text: They painted the jail cell pink, and not just any pink. A scientist mixes exactly one pint of red into a gallon of white and makes the guards repaint the whole thing because the first coat was the wrong shade. The guards are thrilled. Barbie's going to love it in here. Then, he gives them one strange rule. Every prisoner who goes in comes out after exactly 15 minutes, and he waits at the door with a stopwatch. So, the first guy they throw in is the biggest inmate in the building, 300 [music] lb of tattoos laughing at the walls. But, when they pull him out 15 minutes later, the scientist asks the skinniest guard there to arm wrestle him, and the guard slams his hand down in 2 seconds. Wait, what? Well, nobody can explain it. But, within a year, jails all over the country are painting their cells by the truckload. Until one night, a guard forgets about the guy in the pink cell. At 15 minutes, he's sitting quietly. At 20, he's pacing. And by the time they open the door, he's trying to rip the bench out of the floor. You see, the [music] scientist swore this pink drained the fight out of anyone in 15 minutes. So, jails used it to calm their most violent prisoners. But, it only works for 15 minutes. Leave someone in any longer, and it does the exact

title: Why the Second Draw Always Wins
text: The fastest gun in the West had one rule, never draw first. Imagine you're standing in the street at noon staring down a guy everyone calls Slow Eddie. His hands are at his sides, he hasn't even looked at his gun, and he just nods [music] at you and says, "After you." So, you grab for your gun faster than you've ever moved in your life. Yet, you're face down in the dirt before it clears the holster. How is that possible? Eddie isn't even fast. He'd lose a race to the saloon against a guy carrying two beers. But, men ride in from three states away to duel him, and every one [music] of them goes down the exact same way. The only weird thing anyone ever notices is that Eddie never looks at your face. He just stares at your hand. You see, think about the last time your phone slid off a table. You caught it before you even realized it was falling because you never decided to catch it, your body just did. But, when you went for your gun, you had to decide the exact moment to draw, and that tiny decision slowed your hand down. Eddie never decides anything. He just waits for your hand to twitch and lets his body react [music] on its own.

title: Why Sailors Carried Storm Oil
text: He poured cooking oil into the sea, with a pirate ship so close behind them he could hear the pirates laughing. His captain grabs him by the collar and goes, "We're about to get boarded, and you're making soup?" But he doesn't even look up. He just points at the black clouds. "Steer into the storm." The captain yells that they'll never survive it, and all he gets back is, "Trust the oil." But then a grappling hook clangs off the railing. So the captain turns the wheel and the pirates couldn't be happier. Why waste a cannonball when the storm will do it for free? Deeper in, the waves get taller than the mast, and the crew is tying themselves to anything bolted down, but he's still pouring, a little at a time, always on the side the wind is coming from. Then the pirates swing in to board, and up ahead a wave big enough to swallow both ships rises out of the dark. You see, sailors really carried oil just for this. They called it storm oil. Ever blown on a bowl of soup? The broth ripples, but the oily spots stay perfectly smooth, because your breath can't grab [music] them, and a wave can't crash if the wind can't grab it. So when the wave reaches their oily patch of sea, it just lifts the ship and sets it down. And 50 yards behind, it curls over and drops straight onto the pirates'

title: Your Brain's Secret Idea Zone
text: If you fall asleep holding two steel balls, you might wake up a genius. You see, first you put two metal plates on the floor, sit down right above them, and hold a steel ball in each hand. Then, you just let yourself drift off. Now, here's the weird part. The second you fall asleep, your hands go limp, the balls smash into the plates, and the noise jolts you awake. Sounds like the worst nap ever, but Thomas Edison was rumored to do it on purpose. That's because right before deep sleep, your brain hits a strange halfway state called hypnagogia, where it starts connecting ideas it never would while you're awake. Normally, you sink right past it and forget everything. But the crash yank you out right in the middle of it. So, you wake up holding the idea instead of the balls.

title: An Unstoppable Spear vs an Unbreakable Shield
text: A blacksmith sold a spear that could pierce anything to one king, and a shield that nothing could pierce to his worst enemy. The two kingdoms had been at war for a hundred years, and now each king finally had the weapon to end it. So both armies marched to the same field, the spear at the front of one and the shield at the front of the other. Then nobody moved. A whole week went by with 10,000 soldiers just staring at two pieces of metal. One night each king secretly sent a messenger to the blacksmith with the same question, which one is real? And to both of them he gave the same answer, attack and find out. You see, a spear that pierces anything and a shield nothing can pierce can't both exist. So the blacksmith made both out of plain old iron, knowing neither king would dare be the first to find out. And that's how he ended the war.

title: This Shape Saved Roller Coasters
text: He bent the roller [music] coaster's loop out of shape. You see, it's the first ride ever to go upside down, and it cost him everything. So, of course, his rival copies it bolt for bolt. [music] But, the night before opening, his test dummy comes back crushed like a soda can. But, he can't miss the opening. So, he grabs a hammer and beats the bottom into a long, lazy curve. Does he know what he's doing? Not really. His rival laughs, then sneaks in and cranks the sides together until the loop is tall and skinny, so the first cart will snap like a twig. The next morning, the town lines up at the rival's perfect circle, and the rival climbs in front to show off. The owner climbs into his, and as his cart tips over the first hill, he finally sees the tall, skinny loop ahead. But, it's too late. You see, [music] a car can creep around a hairpin turn at five, but take it at 60 and it flips. A cart is fastest at the bottom of a loop, and a perfect circle puts a hairpin right there, which is what crushed the dummy. But, his hammer made the bottom gentle, and the rival's squeeze moved the hairpin up top, where the cart is crawling. So, he floats over without a scratch. Just as the rival's cart hits the bottom of that perfect circle.

title: How Mine Salting Worked
text: He loaded the shotgun with gold and fired it into the walls of the mine. [music] His buddy just watches the gold vanish into the rock. So, we're shooting gold into a gold mine? You see, it's called salting. He's dug this mine for 10 years and found nothing but rock. And tomorrow, a rich guy is coming to buy it. So, he spent his last 100 bucks on gold dust instead. Next morning, the rich guy rolls up in a white suit and bangs his head on the first beam. But he's brought an expert, and the expert isn't stupid. He smashes a chunk of wall, swirls it in a pan, and gold flakes spin to the bottom. But under his magnifying glass, every flake is flat. Somebody shot this gold into the wall, but the rich guy just laughs. Why would anyone shoot gold into a wall? That's insane. And his buddy nods. Completely insane. So, the rich guy pays up. And while those two bolt with the money, he stays behind and pulls a stick of dynamite out of his suit. He's never mined a day in his life. So, he just lights it, tosses [music] it down the tunnel like a firecracker, and runs. And when the dust clears, there's a vein of real gold as thick as your arm, 10 ft past where the last guy gave up.

title: Why Humans Can't Pick Random Numbers
text: If you ever fake a number, there's a way to tell a human made it up. A man stole $2 million [music] with fake checks, made every amount look totally random, and still got caught. But how? Well, picture a building with 19 floors. Step into the elevator and look at the buttons. Floors two through nine each start with a different number, but floor one and 10 all the way up to 19 all start with a one. That's more than half the buttons. Real numbers work like that elevator. So, ones show up way more than anything else. On top of that, real randomness is streaky. Flip a coin 100 times, and you'll usually get six heads in [music] a row. His checks mostly began with a seven, eight, or nine, and he avoided doubles to make them look random. But truly random numbers are the opposite. So, no matter how random you try to make yours, there's almost always a way to

title: Why Cashiers Keep Winning The Lottery
text: He scanned a customer's lottery ticket, saw it had won a million dollars, and said, "Sorry, man, not a winner." The guy just shrugs, says, "Story of my life," and walks out. The second the door closes, the cashier is elbow-deep in the trash can, fishing the ticket back out and tucking it into his wallet like it's been his all along. By midnight, he's already bought a boat, a mansion, and a whole new set of friends, at least in his head. So, the next morning, he drives 2 hours to the lottery office, slides the ticket under the glass, and the lady at the counter smiles and says, "Wow, congratulations! Just wait right here." So, he waits. 5 minutes go by, then 10, until finally a door opens behind him. In walks the guy from the store, except now he's wearing a suit with a badge on his belt, followed by two police officers. You see, in real life, lotteries noticed that store clerks were winning way more often than everyone else, which is statistically a little suspicious. So, they started printing winning tickets as bait and sending undercover agents into stores pretending to be regular customers.

title: The Ancient Jar That Warned an Empire
text: He put a bronze ball in a dragon's mouth and told the emperor if this ever falls out, run. The whole court burst out laughing. You see, there were eight dragons coiled around a giant bronze jar, each holding a ball over a frog's open mouth. But the emperor had the biggest army in the world and he wasn't about to run from a jar. Weeks later, a ball fell, but nothing happened. Not even a ripple in the emperor's mind. Now they laughed even harder. The emperor called it the world's most expensive toy and threw the inventor out of the city, jar and all. So, he dragged it up a hill outside the walls and lived there alone. Then, one night, a ball dropped. Then another. Then all eight at once. He ran to the city gates screaming for everyone to get out. "Hey, it's the toy guy. Did your frogs get hungry again?" The guards laughed him all the way back up the hill. The next morning, the palace was a pile of rubble. Inside the jar hung a heavy pendulum with a rod pointing at each [music] dragon. The slightest nudge and the pendulum swung into a rod, the rod snapped the dragon's jaw open, and the ball dropped. One ball meant a nudge from far [music] away. All eight meant the biggest earthquake the empire had ever seen was right underneath them.

title: What If Humans Invented Teleportation?
text: When humans invent teleportation, billions of people will die and nobody will even notice. Imagine stepping into a glass pod in New [music] York as a blue light scans every single atom in your body and 1 second later, you step out in Tokyo. Within a year, nobody flies anymore and people teleport to work, to see family, even to grab lunch on the other side of the world. But nobody ever asks what actually happens inside that pod. Then one day, a machine glitches. You arrive in Tokyo like always, but somehow you're still standing in New York, too. Now [music] there are two of you, both completely sure they're the real one and the you in New York starts asking a terrifying question. If you never left this time, [music] then where did you go every other morning? Because the machine never moved anyone. It scans [music] you, deletes you and builds a perfect copy on the other side with your face, your memories and the feeling that you just walked through a door. Every trip, the real you died and nobody noticed because the copy always says the trip was perfect. So be honest, would you still [music] step inside?

title: The Town Built Around a Button
text: There's a button in the middle of town and nobody's allowed to press it. The whole town is built around it in perfect circles, every house [music] facing the center where the button sits under a glass case with two guards who never take their eyes off it. Around all of it is a wall so tall nobody's ever seen over it. At night, a glow comes from the other side and every year it gets a little dimmer. But Gary's always noticed two weird things. Under the glass, there are 47 tiny scratches nobody can explain and the statue of the town's founders has a woman who looks exactly like his mom. So when his friends bet him five bucks he won't press it, he can't say no. At 3:00 in the morning, the guard swap shifts and he's got about 30 seconds. He lifts the glass, holds his breath and presses it, but nothing happens. Just a tiny scratching sound under the glass. But as he walks home, the glow over the wall is brighter than it's ever been. The next morning, Gary wakes up in the grass. The houses are gone, the guards are gone, and the whole town is standing in an empty field around the button staring at it like they've never seen it before. Around the button, there are 48 scratches. Then his mom steps out of the crowd and says, "Nobody touches this. We'll build our town right here."

title: How Painkillers Actually Work
text: How do painkillers know where the pain is? You swallow one for a headache, and then what? Does it pull out a little map? All you know is it melts in your stomach, slips into your blood, and 20 minutes later, your headache's gone. So, how does a pill with no brain find the one spot that hurts? Well, picture your body as a house with thousands of rooms and a smoke alarm in every single one. When you get hurt, the alarm in that room starts screaming, and that's the pain you feel. Now, here comes the painkiller. It kicks the front door in and rips the batteries out of every single alarm in the house. Every other alarm was already silent, so the only one you notice go quiet is the one in your head.

title: Why Drivers Started Filming The Road
text: He slammed the brakes on the highway, and the car behind him smashes right into his [music] bumper. He climbs out holding his neck and limping because he figures whoever hits you from behind always gets the blame. And sure enough, their insurance pays for his car, his doctor, and a nice fat check for all that pain he's in. So, the next week he does it again with a different car. He picks them carefully. A guy on his phone, a kid who just got his license, anyone driving a little too close. Then, he brings a buddy who drives right beside you so you can't swerve. The money comes in so fast he buys a nicer car just to crash that one, too. Eventually, the insurance company starts calling. "Sir, this is your fifth neck injury this year." "Yeah, I've got a really weak neck." But, it's his word against the guy who hit him, and he's counting on everyone blaming the guy in the back. Then, one rainy morning he picks a quiet guy in an old car, slams on his brakes, and out he comes clutching his neck. But, the quiet guy doesn't yell, and he doesn't even get out. He just points at a little box taped to his windshield. It's a camera, and it filmed an empty road and a man braking for absolutely nothing. And that's how the dashcam was

title: The Window That Breaks Japan's Gambling Law
text: Gambling is illegal in Japan. Yet, there's a gambling hall on almost every street. Inside, thousands of machines are flashing and screaming while people carry out buckets full of steel balls. Police stroll right past the door, but nobody ever gets arrested. So, you win a bucket yourself and try to cash it in. But, the counter won't give you a single yen. Instead, you can pick cookies, chocolate, a bottle of shampoo, or a few tiny plastic tokens. The guy in front of you takes the tokens and heads straight outside. You follow him around the corner to a little window in a wall with no sign. You see, that isn't part of the gambling hall. It's technically a separate shop that just [music] happens to buy those exact tokens. So, the hall only ever gives out prizes and the shop is just buying one. He slides the tokens through, a hand slides over cash, and on paper, nobody gambled.

title: Would You Upload Your Brain?
text: If you took your brain out and put it in a jar, you die, but your brain wouldn't. Without blood, it loses millions of neurons every minute. But drop it in a jar, hook it up to a machine pumping in oxygen, and it could keep firing, maybe even thinking. Problem is, it would still get old. So, some scientists want to skip the jar. Every memory you have is just a pattern of connections. Copy that pattern into a computer, and you'd technically be immortal. Well, unless someone trips over the power cable. And it's already happening. This year, a company copied a fruit fly's entire brain into a computer, gave it a virtual body, and switched it on. It just started walking around looking for food. It had no idea it wasn't real. The catch? To copy yours, they'd have to pump your brain full of chemicals while you're still alive, then slice it a thousand times thinner than a hair. One company actually offered it. The procedure was 100% fatal. People signed up anyway. Here's the creepy part. Even if it works, the thing that wakes up in the computer remembers your whole life. It swears it's you. But you're still lying on the table. So, would you still sign up?

title: The Scientist's Insane Time Test
text: A scientist dropped people [music] off a tower just to find out what happens to time right before you die. Apparently, when you're terrified, your brain speeds up so much that the whole world slows down. People who survived crashes swear everything went into slow motion. So, before they fell, he strapped a little screen to each of their wrists that flashed numbers way too fast to read. If time really slowed down, they'd be able to read them as they were falling. When they landed, every one of them swore the fall took way longer than it really did. But, when he asked them what number they saw, not one of them could tell him. You see, when you're frightened, your brain records way more detail than normal. So, when you replay it later, it feels like it all happened in slow motion.

title: How One Cart Stopped an Entire Army
text: He drilled 82 holes into the wood because down the hill an army is marching straight for his fort. And while everyone else sharpens swords, he's in the corner still drilling. His commander asks, are we fighting them or grating cheese? But it gets weirder. He bolts the [music] wood onto a cart and into every hole goes something long and thin wrapped in paper, each with a string. Then he twists all the strings into one rope nobody's allowed to touch. One soldier reaches for it and he slaps his hand so hard the whole fort hears it. That night it pours. So [music] he throws his coat over the cart and lies on top of it like a human umbrella. One drop gets in there and we're all dead. The next morning ladders slam against the walls and the army charges. Everyone screams at him to do something, but he just watches them get closer and closer until they're packed shoulder to shoulder, close enough to see their teeth. That's when he rips off the coat and lights the rope. The spark races down it and splits into 82 [music] tiny flames and each one hits a tube of gunpowder strapped to an arrow, turning every one of them into a rocket. All 82 blast off the cart at once, flying every which way. But with the army packed that tight, not a single [music] one misses.

title: This Knight Found the Ultimate Loophole
text: A knight paid a priest to forgive a crime he hadn't committed yet. You see, the priest was traveling from town to town selling forgiveness for coins. Lying had a price, stealing had a price, and the worse the sin, the more you paid. People lined up for hours to drop [music] their money into his huge iron chest. So, the knight stepped up and asked to be forgiven for something he was planning to do next week. The priest hesitated, charged him extra, and stamped the paper anyway. A few days later, the priest left town through the forest with the chest so full it took two men to carry it. That's where the knight was waiting. He took every last coin, and when the priest screamed that he'd go to hell for it, the knight just held up the paper. The crime he paid to be forgiven for was robbing the man [music] who sold it to him.

title: Levels of Pirate Cannonballs
text: If your ship got hit by a cannonball, you'd actually be one of the lucky ones. In the 1700s, the navy's round shot would smash through a pirate ship's wall and turn it into a storm of splinters that tore through half the crew. The pirates couldn't afford proper ammo, so they fired back with langrage, which is a fancy word for literal garbage. But the navy had a nastier idea called hotshot. They shoveled cannonballs into a furnace until they glowed red, carried them over with giant tongs, [music] and dropped them in behind a soaking wet plug so the gunpowder wouldn't go off early. The [music] ball buried itself deep in the pirate ship's hull, and a few minutes later, the whole ship lit up from the inside like a giant lantern. Not to be outdone, the pirates fired back with the carcass, a hollow cannonball [music] packed with burning tar and punched full of holes so it spat fire the whole way over and turned the entire navy ship into a torch. Eventually, ships advanced from wood to iron, and the fireballs just bounced off. So, America built the Rodman gun, a cannon that fired a single ball weighing over a thousand pounds made to punch in an iron warship big enough to sink it in one shot.

title: The Burglar Who Only Moved Furniture
text: A man snuck into a family's house every night and moved every single thing 1 in to the left. The first night, nobody notices because who measures their couch? But by the end of the week, the fridge is blocking the back door [music] and the dad is pretty sure he's losing his mind. So, they call the police. The officer looks at the couch, then at the dad, and goes, "So, someone broke in to move your furniture an inch?" He laughs all the way back to his car. They start locking every door and window at night, but every morning everything has still crept a little further until the bed is pressed up against the wall. At this point, their daughter swears she hears something sliding across the floor at 3:00 a.m. So, the dad camps out on the couch with a baseball bat ready to catch whoever's doing this. He wakes up the next morning and the couch is 1 in to the left with him still [music] on it. By the end of the month, the couch is halfway across the living room and the family can't take it anymore. They sell the house for half what they paid and the buyer is him. You see, he'd sold them that house a year earlier and kept one key. So, all it took was a month of sliding furniture to buy it back at half the price.

title: Oh Nah
text: Welcome, sir, to my shop of curiosities. >> Yeah, can I get that monkey's paw? >> Choose your wishes carefully. >> Oh, I don't want any wishes. One extra large bottle of lube, please.

title: Every Memory Has a Price
text: He sold his happiest memory to a stranger behind a counter. You see, memories are money here. There's a shop on every corner that'll buy one right out of your skull. Landlords take rent and birthdays and a bag of groceries costs the day you learn to ride a bike. The city is split in two by a giant wall. On one side, the rich just buy everyone else's summers. So some guy over there has been to the Bahamas 300 times without leaving his couch. On the other side, people stare at old photos of themselves smiling with no idea why. And since the rich only want the good stuff, the happier the memory, the more it pays. Jerry only sold his to cover [music] rent. But that same week, his little brother gets sick. And every night in the hospital, he begs for the same bedtime story. The summer they caught a frog the size of a football at the lake, but the medicine costs way more than rent. So Jerry goes back and sells that summer for a week of it. The best birthday he ever had pays for the surgery. And soon he's selling whole years until [music] his head is mostly bad days and bus rides. His brother keeps getting worse until there's only one good year left. And the guy behind the counter stares at him and says, "Kid, [music] you sell this, there's nothing happy left in there." He sells it anyway and it pays for everything. A week later, his brother sits up in bed cured [music] and says, "Hey Jerry, tell me the frog story." And Jerry has no idea who this kid is. He sold [music] every happy year he ever had and his brother was in every single one.

title: This Tree Hates You
text: If you ever sit under this tree, it can kill you. Imagine you're stranded on a beach and it's the only tree in sight. It's called the manchineel. It looks completely harmless with little green apples hanging from the branches, but there's a big red X painted on its trunk and you're about to find out why. The first night, a storm rolls in. Naturally, you run under the tree for cover. Big mistake. You see, every leaf on this tree is full of a milky sap and the rain carries it straight onto your skin. Within minutes, you're covered in blisters. This sap is so strong, it can strip the paint off a car. Lesson learned. By the next morning though, you're starving and those little apples smell incredible. One bite actually tastes sweet for about a second. Then, your mouth starts burning and it feels [music] like you swallowed fire. At this point, nature calls. The only thing around to use is a handful of big soft leaves. Yeah, same sap, same blisters, just in a much worse place. When nightfall is, you're freezing. Fortunately, you have plenty of wood. Unfortunately, it's from the same tree. The second it catches, the smoke turns toxic. It burns your eyes until you can't see a thing and every breath scorches your lungs. So, if you're ever stranded on a beach, maybe just sit in the sand.
